backlog.spec: Replace construct_packing with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) over 78 variables (x,y,r per circle). Objective -sum(r). Constraints: r_i<=x_i<=1-r_i, same for y, and pairwise (xi-xj)^2+(yi-yj)^2-(ri+rj)^2>=0 with analytic Jacobians. Start from the existing ring layout with radii from compute_max_radii. maxiter 500. Finally shrink radii by 1e-12 and recompute safe radii so the packing is valid.
backlog.title: SLSQP joint optimize centers+radii from ring init

backlog.spec: Fixed seed np.random.default_rng(0). Loop many random initial center sets (uniform in the square, radii 0.05 start) and run SLSQP with vectorized constraints and Jacobians for each; keep the best valid result. Stop at a time budget of 200 s using time.time().
backlog.title: Multi-start SLSQP with random seeds

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, alternate: fix centers and solve the LP max sum r subject to r_i<=border distance and r_i+r_j<=d_ij using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Then perturb centers via SLSQP again. Repeat a few rounds and keep the best.
backlog.title: LP radii refinement for fixed centers

backlog.spec: Starting from the best SLSQP solution, do basin hopping: perturb a random subset of 1-4 circles' centers by Gaussian noise of sigma 0.05, re-run SLSQP (short maxiter 100), accept if the sum improves (or with Metropolis temperature 0.002). Run for about 200 s with a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Basin hopping on centers

backlog.spec: Initialise centers with a perturbed grid of rows (e.g. 6,5,5,5,5 circles) with random jitter of 0.02, then refine with SLSQP. Try several row patterns (5,5,5,5,6; 4,5,4,5,4,4; 6,5,6,5,4) and keep the best.
backlog.title: Hex-grid-based init with rows 5-5-5-5-5 plus one

backlog.spec: Initialise with 4 larger circles (r~0.15) near the corners, edge circles of medium radius (r~0.1) along the sides, and small circles filling the interior at random. Run SLSQP. Multi-start with different random interior seeds.
backlog.title: Corner-big-circles init

backlog.spec: Stage 1: minimize -sum r + mu * (sum of squared overlap violations + wall violations) with L-BFGS-B, for mu increasing 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4 and 1e5. Stage 2: polish with SLSQP. Use many random inits and keep the best.
backlog.title: Penalty-method gradient descent then SLSQP

backlog.spec: Start with all radii equal to a target R and run a repulsion physics model to resolve overlaps. Then free the radii and optimize with SLSQP. Try R in a sweep from 0.08 to 0.11 and pick the best.
backlog.title: Radius-size schedule annealing

backlog.spec: Annealing loop: move one circle's center by a Gaussian step (temperature-scaled), evaluate the sum of radii via a fast LP (linprog highs). Accept by Metropolis. Cool geometrically over about 3000 iterations, then polish with SLSQP.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing on centers with LP evaluation

backlog.spec: From the current best, remove the smallest circle and reinsert it at the largest hole (the point maximizing the distance to the nearest circle edge, found on a grid of candidate points). Re-run SLSQP. Repeat for each of the k smallest circles and accept improvements.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle moves

backlog.spec: Speed up SLSQP by including only pair constraints for pairs within distance 0.4 and use numpy vectorized constraint and Jacobian functions. This allows many more restarts within the time budget. Use 2 phases: coarse (maxiter 150) on many starts, then full polish on the top 5.
backlog.title: Vectorized constraints with sparse neighbor pruning

backlog.spec: Impose a mirror symmetry about x=0.5 or the diagonal: optimize 13 free circles plus their mirror images (or some on the axis). Use SLSQP on the reduced variables, then release the symmetry and polish with full SLSQP.
backlog.title: Symmetry-constrained search

backlog.spec: Use scipy minimize method trust-constr with NonlinearConstraint objects and sparse Jacobians, starting from the best SLSQP result, to polish to a higher precision. Compare with SLSQP and keep the better valid one.
backlog.title: Trust-constr alternative solver

backlog.spec: Maximize sum r + t*sum log(slack) over all constraints slacks with L-BFGS-B, increasing t^-1 progressively (t from 1 to 1e-6). The start is feasible (small radii at random centers). Finish by SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior-point approach

backlog.spec: At the end, recompute the radii by an LP for fixed centers, then multiply them by (1-1e-12) and subtract 1e-13. Verify all constraints in double precision, and if any pair fails, shrink the offending radii until valid. Return the sum computed with np.sum of the final radii.
backlog.title: Final validity safeguard

backlog.spec: Parametrise a layout as a ring structure (radii of ring and angular offsets for rings with counts 1,6,9,10 etc.) and use scipy differential_evolution with the LP-evaluated sum. Then refine the best with SLSQP on all variables.
backlog.title: Differential evolution on a low-dim parametrisation

backlog.spec: Initialise the radii as a decreasing function of the distance from the centre (r = 0.13 at the centre to 0.07 at the edges), with centers from a jittered hex lattice scaled to the square. Run SLSQP. Multi-start over jitter seeds.
backlog.title: Weighted-size init: big center, small edge

backlog.spec: Sample 26 random points and run several Lloyd/Voronoi relaxations (approximated on a 200x200 grid) with weights, to get evenly spread centers. Then run SLSQP. Do many seeds and keep the best.
backlog.title: Lloyd-style centroid relaxation init

backlog.spec: Loop: take the best solution, add Gaussian noise sigma in {0.01, 0.02, 0.04} to all centers, set radii to 0.8 times the safe radii, re-run SLSQP, and keep it if better. Run until the 200 s budget with a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-repolish from best (kick)

backlog.spec: In the best solution, pick two circles with different radii and swap their centers. Set the radii to the LP solution and repolish with SLSQP. Accept if improved. Iterate over random pairs.
backlog.title: Swap circles of different sizes

backlog.spec: Set ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=2000 in SLSQP, and scale variables so that constraints are normalized. Rerun polish from the best. This squeezes the last 1e-6 out of the sum.
backlog.title: Increase SLSQP precision settings

backlog.spec: First solve the max-min-distance (equal circle) packing of 26 points via SLSQP on (centers, r) with a common r. Then use the result as the init for the variable-radii SLSQP. Add random perturbations for diversity.
backlog.title: Two-pass: equal radii then free

backlog.spec: Physics model: circles with radii growing at rate proportional to free space while repelled by overlapping neighbours (Lubachevsky–Stillinger style) for 2000 steps with decreasing step size. Then SLSQP polish the result.
backlog.title: Overlap-tolerant soft radii growth

backlog.spec: Place a layout of rows alternating between 5 and 6 circles with different row spacing and random radii perturbations, plus an extra circle placed in a gap. Try combinatorial variants of row counts totalling 26 and polish each with SLSQP.
backlog.title: Hybrid rows layout with 4 corner circles

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, identify circles with no active contacts (rattlers). Move them to a random location in the largest hole and re-optimize. Repeat as long as the sum improves.
backlog.title: Constraint-activity-guided restarts

backlog.spec: Add a small term lambda*sum((r - mean r)^2) with lambda decaying 1e-2 to 0 over a few SLSQP stages to guide the early search toward balanced configurations. Remove it for the final stage.
backlog.title: Radius-sum regularization toward a mean

backlog.spec: Maintain 4 chains with kick magnitudes 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08 each running perturb-and-polish with SLSQP. Occasionally swap the states between chains by a Metropolis rule. Return the global best.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering of kicks

backlog.spec: Initialise with circles in groups: 4 corner ones of r≈0.13, 12 edge ones of r≈0.1, 10 interior ones of r≈0.1, positions random within their zones. Run SLSQP, and multi-start across seeds.
backlog.title: Use best-known-like structure: 3 radii classes

backlog.spec: Wrap the whole search in a loop using time.time(), stopping new starts at 200 s. Cycle init types (random, grid, ring, hex), keep the global best valid solution, and fall back to the ring init if everything fails.
backlog.title: Time-budgeted restart manager

backlog.spec: Optimize over the centers only using a smooth objective: the sum of the LP-optimal radii approximated by a softmin. Use autograd-free finite differences with L-BFGS-B over 52 variables, then polish with SLSQP over all 78.
backlog.title: Pairwise-distance-based radii bound lift

backlog.spec: After the basin-hopping phase, add a move: take the incumbent solution, remove the 1-2 smallest-radius circles, and reinsert each at a point maximizing distance to all other circles and walls (estimate by sampling 2000 random points and picking the one with the largest min of (distance to other circle edges, wall distance)). Set its radius to a small value like 0.02, then run SLSQP polish (maxiter 150). Accept if the sum improves. Use this as 40% of the kick moves in the basin hopping loop.
backlog.title: Smallest-circle relocate into largest hole

backlog.spec: Add a phase of about 40s that searches packings symmetric about the main diagonal. Free variables: 13 circles are paired with their mirror images (x,y)->(y,x), and optionally a few circles sit on the diagonal, e.g. 0, 2, 4 on-diagonal with the rest in mirrored pairs. Run the penalty and SLSQP pipeline on the reduced variable set, expand to the full 26 circles, then do a full unconstrained SLSQP polish. Keep the result if it beats the incumbent. Try several on-diagonal counts.
backlog.title: Symmetric-search with diagonal mirror

backlog.spec: Run multistart inits from structured patterns: 4 large corner circles (r about 0.13), 8 medium edge circles (r about 0.1), 14 interior circles (r about 0.09) with jittered hex placement. Randomly choose the pattern's parameters per restart (row offsets, jitter 0.02-0.06). Then run SLSQP directly with maxiter 300. Replace the uniform-random starts for 50% of the multistart time.
backlog.title: Seed from the incumbent with a 3-radius-class init

backlog.spec: Replace the finalize step so it shrinks radii by only 1e-13 relative, rather than 1e-10 absolute. Then verify exactly in double precision. For every pair, check that r_i + r_j <= d, using np.nextafter-style reductions on violators, and check the wall constraints. Only if the check fails, shrink the offending radii by 1e-12 steps. This recovers about 2e-9 and guarantees validity.
backlog.title: Tighter safeguarded final margin

backlog.spec: Replace the basin hopping with an iterated local search from the best solution only. Each iteration picks sigma log-uniformly in [0.01, 0.2] and k in 1..6 circles to perturb, with the kick also resetting radii to 0.9x. Run SLSQP with maxiter 80. Accept only improvements, and every 60 non-improving iterations restart from the best of the top-5 pool. Use a 190s budget.
backlog.title: Long low-temperature kick chain with adaptive sigma

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the top 8 distinct local optima (distinct by sum differing by more than 1e-5). At the end, polish each with SLSQP at ftol 1e-15 and maxiter 1000. Then identify the active constraints (slack under 1e-7), and solve the KKT equality system Newton-style for the active set to reach machine-precision tightness. Return the best.
backlog.title: Trust-constr / active-set refinement of top candidates

backlog.spec: In the penalty function, add a small term lambda*sum(r^2) with a negative sign, which favors uneven radii (lambda from 0.05 down to 0 across the mu schedule). This pushes the optimizer toward the heterogeneous size distributions seen in the best packings. Apply it to half of the multistarts and anneal it to zero before the SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted repulsion regularizer in the penalty stage

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP step, compute the contact graph (pairs with slack under 1e-6). Pick one random contact, delete it by pushing the two circles apart by 0.02 along the contact line, and move a random neighbor of one of them toward a low-density region. Re-run SLSQP. This does targeted topology changes rather than random kicks. Use it as an alternative move in the basin-hopping loop with probability 0.5.
backlog.title: Contact-graph perturbation restarts

backlog.spec: Start by solving for 22 circles with multistart (about 10s). Then add 4 circles one at a time, each at the largest empty hole (sampled farthest-point) with a tiny radius, and re-optimize with SLSQP after each insertion. Repeat with different seeds for the 22-circle base. Use the 26-circle results as additional starts feeding basin hopping.
backlog.title: Staged circle-count growth

backlog.spec: Speed up the SLSQP by including only the pair constraints whose centers are within 0.45 of each other, which is about 40% of the 325 pairs. Then verify all pairs at the end and re-solve with the full set if any are violated. The cheaper iterations should allow roughly 2-3x more basin-hopping steps in the same 140s. Use a different seed offset for the hopping chain.
backlog.title: Batch SLSQP with sparse neighbor constraints

backlog.spec: Replace half of the random multistart initialisations with structured row layouts: choose row counts from a list such as (5,5,5,5,6), (4,5,4,5,4,4), (6,5,5,5,5), jitter x positions slightly (sigma 0.01), space rows evenly in y, set initial radii to 0.08, then run the existing penalty L-BFGS-B stages and SLSQP polish. Randomly permute row-count order per start. Keep the basin hopping phase from the best result.
backlog.title: Hex-row structured inits with SLSQP

backlog.spec: For multistart, parametrise 13 free circles plus their reflections across the diagonal x=y (or 13 pairs mirrored across x=0.5). Optimise the symmetric problem with SLSQP over only half the variables, which has a smaller search space. Then take the best 5 symmetric solutions and release the symmetry with a full 78-variable SLSQP polish followed by basin hopping. Allocate about 60s to symmetric search.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search then free polish

backlog.spec: In the basin hopping phase, add a move: pick the 1-3 circles with smallest radii, remove them, and reinsert each at a random point sampled from the largest empty holes (take 2000 random points and choose the one maximising the distance to the nearest remaining circle surface and borders). Set the new radius to 0.5 of that clearance, then SLSQP repolish. Use it with probability 0.4 per step, and accept with the existing Metropolis rule.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circles

backlog.spec: Take the best solution found after the multistart phase, sort the radii, and cluster them into 3 classes (large, medium, small) by k-means in 1D. Generate new starts by re-randomising the center positions while assigning initial radii from the class values, with class membership drawn in the same proportions. Place large circles near the interior and small ones near edges and corners. Run the penalty stages with these radii as the start, then SLSQP. Use 30s of the budget.
backlog.title: Radius-class seeded init from the incumbent structure

backlog.spec: Before the penalty L-BFGS-B stages, run 300 steps of an energy-minimisation pre-stage. It uses the potential sum over pairs of (w_i*w_j/d)^2 with random weights w drawn lognormally (sigma 0.4), plus a wall repulsion term. The result spreads circles into a nonuniform arrangement with a size distribution. Set the initial radii to 0.4*w*mean spacing. Then run the usual penalty and SLSQP stages. Apply it to 70% of the multistart starts.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted repulsion pre-stage

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best 3 distinct solutions and polish each with SLSQP at maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-15. Use only near-active constraints (pairs with distance less than r_i+r_j+0.05) via a sparse neighbour list rebuilt twice. Choose the best result after the safe finalize. This tightens the active-set convergence and may gain around 1e-8.
backlog.title: Trust-constr / larger-iteration SLSQP final polish

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed sigma 0.05 basin hopping with a chain whose sigma adapts: start at 0.03, multiply by 1.1 after each rejection and by 0.8 after each acceptance, clipped to [0.005, 0.15]. Number of perturbed circles is drawn from 1..6. Use temperature 0.0005. Reset sigma to 0.03 and restart the chain from the best solution after 150 consecutive non-improving steps. Run for the whole remaining time budget.
backlog.title: Adaptive-sigma long kick chain from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Speed up multistart by making the SLSQP constraint function use only pairs within distance 0.35 of each other, recomputed at the start of each run from the penalty-stage output. This reduces the 325 pair constraints to about 100. Reduce the penalty stage to mu in (30,1000,1e5) with maxiter 150. Aim for 4-5x more starts in the 60s phase. Verify the final solution against all pairs in finalize.
backlog.title: Batch of many short SLSQP runs with neighbour-pruned constraints

backlog.spec: Generate starts with four large circles (radius about 0.13-0.18) placed in the four corners, at (r,r) etc., with 1-2 additional large circles near the center. Fill the remaining 20-21 circles at random positions with radius 0.07. Then run the penalty stage, with the corner circles' centers free to move, and the SLSQP polish. Run for about 40% of the multistart time, in competition with the random starts.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored large circle init

backlog.spec: Change rng seed to a loop over several seeds in the multistart phase: split the 200s budget into 3 independent runs (multistart 25s plus basin hopping 45s each, different default_rng seeds 1,2,3), keep the best valid result overall. Purpose is to escape the single basin reached with seed 0.
backlog.title: Seed-sweep restart from incumbent-like structure

backlog.spec: Replace the basin hopping loop with one that adapts sigma: start at 0.03, multiply by 0.9 after a rejection streak of 10 and reset to 0.05 after an acceptance of improvement; use temperature 0.0005; always restart the chain from the best after 60 non-improving steps. Perturb 1-3 circles per step. Keep SLSQP maxiter 100.
backlog.title: Adaptive-sigma long kick chain

backlog.spec: For half of multistart starts initialise radii by class: 4 corner circles r=0.12, ~8 edge circles r=0.10 placed near the boundary, remaining ~14 interior circles r=0.08 on a jittered hex lattice (noise 0.02), centers jittered. Skip the penalty stage and go directly to SLSQP with maxiter 300.
backlog.title: Three-radius-class structured init

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, pick the 3 circles with smallest radii, delete them, and reinsert each at a random location among the top Voronoi-like vertices (computed by evaluating a 60x60 grid and choosing points with largest distance-to-nearest-circle-surface). Initial radius for them 0.03. Use only for 30% of steps, run SLSQP maxiter 150.
backlog.title: Bigger-circle-biased removal and reinsertion with SLSQP-only

backlog.spec: After the search, take best v and run SLSQP with ftol 1e-15 and maxiter 1000, then a final LP (scipy linprog highs) on radii with centers fixed, maximising sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij-1e-13 and wall constraints; accept if the sum is higher and finalize check passes. Reserve the last 15s for this.
backlog.title: Dual-precision final polish

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, build constraints only for pairs with center distance < 0.35 at the start of each SLSQP call (about 120 pairs instead of 325), then validate full constraints afterwards in finalize and discard if violated. This speeds each hop 2-3x, allowing many more hops in the same budget.
backlog.title: Cheaper neighbour-pruned SLSQP for many more hops

backlog.spec: Generate starts from a 5x5 square grid (25 circles) plus one extra circle inserted in a random gap, or from hex rows 5-6-5-6-4 truncated/padded to 26, with jitter 0.03 and radii 0.08. Run SLSQP directly. Use these for 50% of the multistart phase.
backlog.title: Lattice-with-defect inits

backlog.spec: In the multistart penalty stage, maximise sum w_i r_i with w_i random in [0.7,1.3] for the first mu stages, then anneal weights to 1 over the last two mu values. This biases toward different radius distributions and diversifies basins before the true-objective SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Radius-sum-weighted penalty with random objective weights

backlog.spec: For 30s, search packings symmetric under 180-degree rotation about the center (13 pairs, or 12 pairs plus one center circle) by optimising 13 free circles with mirrored constraints via SLSQP on the reduced variables; then expand to all 26 circles and polish freely with SLSQP maxiter 300 plus basin hopping for the rest.
backlog.title: Symmetry-breaking mirror then free polish

backlog.spec: Reduce the multistart phase to 30s, then run basin hopping until 225s with rng seed changed to 12345. Keep the same kick (1-4 centers, sigma 0.05) and SLSQP settings, and keep the finalize shrink margin unchanged. This tests whether a different seed and a longer chain find a better basin.
backlog.title: Long basin hopping from incumbent with new seed

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, use Metropolis temperature 0.0005 instead of 0.002. If there is no improvement of the best for 40 consecutive hops, reset the current state to the best-so-far. This gives a more exploitative search that still escapes stalls.
backlog.title: Sub-threshold acceptance with restarts to best

backlog.spec: As a basin-hopping move, delete the 2 smallest circles. Compute candidate hole locations as Voronoi vertices (scipy.spatial.Voronoi) of the remaining centers plus the square corners, clipped to the square. Choose the 2 candidates with the largest distance to the nearest remaining circle boundary, place the circles there with radius 0.02, and run SLSQP. Use this on 30% of the hops.
backlog.title: Remove-two reinsert-into-holes with Voronoi vertices

backlog.spec: For multistart inits, assign 4 circles radius about 0.13 (large, near the interior), 10 circles radius about 0.11, and 12 circles radius about 0.08. Place the large ones randomly in [0.2,0.8]^2 and the rest uniformly. Jitter, then run the penalty stages and SLSQP as before. Use this on every multistart iteration for 60s.
backlog.title: Three-radius-class seeded init

backlog.spec: In the multistart and in half of the hops, first run SLSQP maximizing sum w_i r_i, with w_i drawn from uniform(0.7,1.3), at maxiter 60. Then run the true objective sum r_i polish from that result. The weights shift the contact graph into different basins.
backlog.title: Randomly weighted objective in SLSQP stage

backlog.spec: Initialize 4 circles near the corners with centers at (r,r) etc. and radius 0.12-0.15. Place 4 more medium circles near the edge midpoints. Scatter the remaining 18 randomly with radius 0.07. Run penalty then SLSQP. Use this for all 60s of multistart, then continue with basin hopping.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored init

backlog.spec: For 40s, sample configurations that are symmetric under the x -> 1-x reflection: 13 free circles plus their mirror images, or 12 mirrored pairs plus 2 circles on x=0.5. Optimize the reduced variables with SLSQP, then break the symmetry by adding noise of 0.003 and run a full free SLSQP polish. Take the best candidate as the start for basin hopping.
backlog.title: Mirror symmetry then free polish

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best solution and run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' using the same constraints and jacobians, xtol 1e-12, maxiter 2000. Then re-run SLSQP with ftol 1e-15 and maxiter 500. Keep whichever result is better after finalize. The finalize margin stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Trust-constr high-precision final polish

backlog.spec: Keep the 6 best distinct local optima found in the multistart. In the hopping phase, with probability 0.3 build a child by taking circles from parent A with x<t and from parent B with x>=t, with t random in [0.3,0.7]. Add or remove circles at random to restore 26, with the radii set to 0.05, and run SLSQP. This is a genetic-style recombination.
backlog.title: Pool-based crossover of two good solutions

backlog.spec: For hop SLSQP, include only the pair constraints whose centre distance is below 0.45 in the starting point, which gives about 3x fewer constraints. Use maxiter 60. After each hop, verify the full constraint set and polish with the full SLSQP only if the hop sum is within 0.003 of the best. This gives about 3-5x more hops in the same time.
backlog.title: Batch many cheap neighbour-pruned hops

backlog.spec: During the multistart phase keep a pool of the top 10 distinct solutions (centers and radii, distinct if the sorted radii differ by more than 1e-4). In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.3 per iteration build a child: pick two pool members, choose a random line through the square (random angle, offset near 0.5), take centers on one side from parent A and on the other side from parent B, fix the count to 26 by dropping the smallest circles or adding random centers, set radii to 0.05 times 0.9, and SLSQP polish. Insert the child into the pool if it is better than the worst member. Keep the final 26 seconds of hopping from the best only.
backlog.title: Crossover of pooled local optima

backlog.spec: In the SLSQP polish of the multistart and hopping phases, replace the objective -sum(r) with -sum(w_i r_i) where w_i = 1 + 0.3*uniform(-1,1) is drawn per run. Then re-polish the result with the true uniform objective (w = 1) for 100 more iterations. This gives different vertices of the feasible set and helps escape the stuck basin. Apply it to 50% of hops.
backlog.title: Randomly weighted objective in SLSQP stage

backlog.spec: After the search ends at about 200s, take the best solution and polish it with scipy trust-constr (vectorised constraints from cons/cjac, gtol 1e-12, maxiter 500), then with SLSQP at ftol 1e-15. Reserve about 25s for this. Keep the result only if the finalized sum is larger. Shrink the radii by 1e-12 relative, and check pair overlaps at double precision before returning.
backlog.title: Trust-constr high-precision polish of top candidates

backlog.spec: For multistart, build hex-like lattices of 5 or 6 rows with row counts that sum to 26 plus 0 to 2 extras. Delete the extras at random positions, or add them at random positions. Jitter the centers by 0.01 and set radii to 0.09. Run SLSQP directly, without the penalty stages. Randomise the row orientation (rows along x or y) and the row counts for each start. Use this for the first 60s of multistart.
backlog.title: Lattice with defect inits

backlog.spec: In basin hopping use a Metropolis temperature of 0.004, which is higher than the current one. Reset the current state to the best-so-far every 150 hops, or after 40 hops without a new best. Use the kick sigma log-uniform in [0.01, 0.1]. Keep the best solution as the return value.
backlog.title: Sub-threshold acceptance with restarts to best

backlog.spec: For 40s, search symmetric packings. Impose x-mirror symmetry (x -> 1-x) with 13 mirrored pairs, or 12 pairs plus 2 circles on the axis x = 0.5. Optimise the reduced variables with SLSQP from random starts and hops. Take the best 5 symmetric solutions, perturb each by sigma 0.005, and run full free SLSQP on them. Compare the results with the incumbent.
backlog.title: Mirror symmetry then free polish

backlog.spec: Multistart variant: fix 4 circles in the corners (centres at (r,r) for r drawn from [0.1,0.2]) and sample 4 larger circles near the middle of the square. Sample the other 18 circles with uniform random centres and radii 0.07. Run the penalty stages and then SLSQP, with all variables free in the SLSQP. Use this for 50% of the multistart starts. Randomise the radius draws for each start.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored large circle init

backlog.spec: From the best solution find the pairs that are in contact (slack below 1e-8). Choose one contact pair at random, move the two circles apart by pushing one by 0.03 along the contact normal to the neighbouring void, shrink both radii by 30%, and SLSQP polish. Also try rotating a 3-circle cluster around its centroid by a random angle up to 60 degrees. Use these in 30% of hops.
backlog.title: Contact-graph removal of one active constraint

backlog.spec: Split the run into 4 independent chains of 50s each (multistart 12s then hopping 38s), using seeds 1, 2, 3, 4 (rng created per chain). At the end pick the best chain's result and polish it with SLSQP at maxiter 300 for the remaining time. This diversifies the basins explored, compared with one 200s chain from seed 0.
backlog.title: Seed sweep with split time budget

backlog.spec: Keep the current pipeline (60s multistart then basin hopping to 200s) but split the 200s budget into 3 independent runs with seeds 1,2,3 (multistart 15s + basin hopping ~50s each), then take the best and spend the remaining time on basin hopping from it. This tests whether the -2.6360 basin is reached from varied starts and gives a chance of a better one.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent with different seed sweep

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best solution and polish it with scipy trust-constr using the same analytic constraint Jacobian (sparse near-neighbour pairs only, gtol 1e-12, maxiter 2000). Finalize the result with the usual shrink margin, and keep it only if the finalized sum is larger than the incumbent's.
backlog.title: Trust-constr high-precision polish

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, replace the SLSQP objective -sum(r) with -sum(w_i r_i), where w_i = 1 + 0.3*N(0,1) clipped to [0.3,1.7], for the first SLSQP pass. Then re-run SLSQP with the true objective from that result. This pushes the solver across different contact structures. Accept on the true sum.
backlog.title: Randomly weighted objective hops

backlog.spec: After basin hopping, take the best packing and identify active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-7). Solve the KKT system for the max-sum-radii problem restricted to this active set with scipy.linalg.lstsq or a Newton iteration on the equality system (d_ij = r_i + r_j, wall gaps = 0), starting from the SLSQP solution, to reach machine-precision contacts. Then recompute radii with a HiGHS LP on the fixed centers, shrink by 1e-12 relative, verify validity strictly, and return it only if the sum is higher than before the polish.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of contact graph

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 replace the local kick with a global affine move. Apply x -> 0.5+(x-0.5)*(1+a) and y -> 0.5+(y-0.5)*(1-a) with a ~ N(0,0.05), plus a small shear. Clip, set radii to 0.8x, and run SLSQP. Alternatively, shift one random row or column band of circles (those within 0.1 of a random x or y) by 0.05 along the band. Accept by the existing criterion.
backlog.title: Anisotropic stretch kicks

backlog.spec: Wrap the whole search in a function taking a seed and a time budget. Run seeds 0, 1 and 2 sequentially with budgets of 15s multistart plus 50s basin hopping each. Then take the best of the three and spend the remaining ~30s on basin hopping from it with small sigma (0.01-0.03). Return the overall best packing after the existing finalize.
backlog.title: Split-budget three-seed run

backlog.spec: Optimise packings in a variable square of side L. Add a variable L, with walls at 0 and L, and maximize sum(r)/L. Equivalently, fix the sum and minimize L. Run it in the multistart SLSQP, then rescale centers and radii by 1/L to the unit square. This changes the landscape so that different basins are reached. Use it for 30% of multistart starts, then polish in the standard unit-square formulation.
backlog.title: Free-boundary relaxation via square rescaling

backlog.spec: For the best packing, compute the SLSQP constraint multipliers (from the active-set least-squares solution of grad f = J^T lambda). Find the pair contacts with the smallest positive multipliers and the circles with the smallest radii. In basin hopping, with probability 0.3 pick one of the three weakest contacts, push the two circles apart by 0.04 along the line of centers, add a random 0.02 jitter to their neighbors, set radii to 0.8x, and re-run SLSQP.
backlog.title: Lagrange-guided removal of weak contacts

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP polish in 30% of multistart starts, run an extra stage maximizing sum(r) + 0.3*min(r) via an auxiliary variable t with constraints t <= r_i, and the objective sum(r) + 0.3 t, for 60 iterations. Then switch to the plain objective sum(r). This lifts the tiny circles and gives a different contact topology. Keep the best result across all starts.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius objective warm start

backlog.spec: In the multistart, before the SLSQP polish, run SLSQP for 60 iterations maximizing sum(r) minus 0.5*sum((r-mean r)^2), which pushes radii toward uniform. Then run the normal SLSQP polish on pure sum(r). This lets the structure form before the radii specialize.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius objective warm start

backlog.spec: Run the basin hopping on a rectangle of aspect ratio a (random in [0.9,1.1]) by scaling the y coordinates and radii constraints. Anneal a toward 1 across the hops. This gives the search a different landscape that is smoothed away at the end. Finish with a hop phase on the true unit square from the best state.
backlog.title: Two-scale square rescaling search

backlog.spec: Run 3 seeds, each with 20s multistart and 30s basin hopping. Take the best of the three. Spend the remaining ~90s on basin hopping from it with a fresh rng. Use the best solution ever seen as the final output.
backlog.title: Time-split multi-seed with elite restart

backlog.spec: After each accepted SLSQP in basin hopping, compute the multipliers from a least-squares solve of the active-constraint gradient system. Pick the active pair constraint with the smallest positive multiplier and push the two circles apart by 0.02 along their axis. Re-run SLSQP and accept if better. Use this as 25% of hops.
backlog.title: Lagrange-guided weak-contact release

backlog.spec: Make no edit to train.py. Run the incumbent once more (seed 0, 60s multistart then basin hopping to 200s) to measure repeatability. If the clock makes results differ, this tells us how much noise there is behind the -2.6360 figure.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move with probability 0.3. Remove the two smallest circles. Compute candidate hole centers as the vertices of the Voronoi diagram of the remaining centers plus the square's reflected boundary points, keeping vertices inside the square. Rank them by clearance (distance to the nearest circle surface or wall). Reinsert the two circles at the two best vertices, which must be well separated, with radius 0.5 times clearance. Then run SLSQP as usual.
backlog.title: Voronoi-vertex reinsertion of two circles

backlog.spec: For half of the multistarts, replace the first penalty stages (mu 10 and 100) with an objective that maximises sum(r) plus 0.05*softmin(r), where softmin is -log(sum(exp(-r/0.01)))*0.01. This pushes small circles to grow early. Drop the softmin term for the later stages and the SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius warm start

backlog.spec: Search over packings in a rectangle of aspect ratio a in [0.85,1.15] with width 1 and height a. Do this for 20s, using SLSQP with the wall constraints set to the rectangle. Then map the best solutions into the unit square by scaling y by 1/a and shrinking the radii to be valid. Finally, polish with the standard unit-square SLSQP and feed the result into basin hopping as the starting state.
backlog.title: Free-boundary square rescaling search

backlog.spec: Reduce SLSQP in basin hopping to maxiter 40 and ftol 1e-9, with pair constraints only for pairs closer than 0.4. This allows about 3x more hops. Every 300 hops, reset the current state to the elite best. Re-polish the best with the full SLSQP at the end. Run 3 chains sequentially with seeds 0, 1 and 2, each with 55s of hopping, and keep the best.
backlog.title: Many cheap hops with elite restart

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move with probability 0.3 that leaves the centers fixed and randomizes the radii. Multiply each radius by lognormal(0, 0.3), then clip to feasibility by the shrink loop. Run SLSQP with a 1e-3 centers trust region (bounds around the current centers) first, then fully free. This lets the optimizer explore different contact graphs that share nearly the same centers.
backlog.title: Perturb radii-only then re-solve

backlog.spec: For 30% of the multistart starts, place 4 circles at the corners, 8 circles along the edges at spacing near 0.25 with jitter 0.02, and the remaining 14 circles on a jittered hexagonal lattice with spacing 0.2 inside [0.2,0.8]^2. Use initial radii 0.12, 0.10 and 0.09 respectively. Run the SLSQP polish directly, skipping the penalty stages. Start basin hopping from the best result of the whole multistart.
backlog.title: Three-class corner/edge/interior seeded SLSQP with big hexagonal interior

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py (resubmit it as is, e.g. with a comment-only edit) to measure run-to-run repeatability of the -2.6360 result. Since the seed is fixed, it also confirms that time-based loop cutoffs do not cause variation.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: During the 60s multistart, keep the top 10 distinct local optima (by sum of radii, distinct if sorted-radii vectors differ by more than 1e-3). After that, for 20s, create children by choosing a random vertical or horizontal cut line at a position in [0.3,0.7]. Take the circles of parent A whose centers lie on one side and those of parent B on the other side. Fix the count to 26 by dropping the smallest circles or adding circles at random positions with radius 0.02. Polish each child with SLSQP, and add it to the pool if it improves on the worst entry. Then continue basin hopping from the best child or the incumbent best, whichever is better.
backlog.title: Pool crossover of local optima

backlog.spec: In 30% of basin-hopping hops, remove the two circles with the smallest radii. Compute the Voronoi vertices of the remaining centers (scipy.spatial.Voronoi) together with the square's corners. Keep only the vertices inside the square. Rank them by the distance to the nearest circle surface (the largest empty holes). Reinsert the two circles at the top two holes, at least 0.1 apart, with radius 0.02. Run the usual SLSQP polish and Metropolis acceptance.
backlog.title: Voronoi-vertex reinsertion of two circles

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP on a packing in a rectangle of width w and height 1/w, with w as an extra variable bounded to [0.8,1.25]. The maximum sum of radii is then optimised over aspect ratio too. For the first 30s of multistart, use this relaxation. Then rescale the result to the unit square by x/=w and y*=w, and re-polish with the normal SLSQP. Take the best of the polished results as a seed for basin hopping, as an alternative to the current best.
backlog.title: Free-boundary square rescaling search

backlog.spec: For each multistart run, apply the SLSQP bounds r<=cap with cap decreasing through 0.16, 0.13, 0.11 and 0.5, warm-starting each stage from the previous one with maxiter 80. Different caps force different size distributions, which favours packings with many medium circles instead of a few large ones. Apply this to half of the starts and compare the results.
backlog.title: Radius-cap annealing schedule in multistart

backlog.spec: Initialise with a jittered hexagonal-like lattice of 16 circles of radius about 0.13, with positions randomly shifted by 0.02. Then greedily add 10 circles at the largest empty holes, found by evaluating a 50x50 grid of distances to the nearest circle surface and walls. Give each new circle a radius equal to 0.9 times the hole size. Run SLSQP. Use this for 40% of the multistart starts, in place of the pure random starts.
backlog.title: Large-seed lattice with gap filling

backlog.spec: In 30% of basin-hopping hops, leave the centers unchanged. Instead, multiply the radii of 3 to 6 randomly chosen circles by a random factor in [0.5,1.5], clip them to be feasible by uniform scaling of the overlapping pairs, and run SLSQP. This changes which contacts are active without moving the centers, which a geometric kick cannot do.
backlog.title: Radii-only perturbation then re-solve in hops

backlog.spec: Spend 150s on basin hopping where each hop runs SLSQP with maxiter 25 on neighbour-pruned constraints (pairs closer than 0.3). Keep the 5 best distinct hop results. Fully polish only those every 20 hops with the full constraint set and maxiter 200. This gives about 3x more hops per unit time. Accept using the full polished values only.
backlog.title: Parallel-batch hops via common-random-number short SLSQP

backlog.spec: In 25% of hops, pick the largest circle and the smallest circle. Swap their radii and centers' radii assignment only (positions stay), then also move the smallest circle's center to a random nearby position within 0.15 of the largest circle's center. Run SLSQP. Put the previous best structure's hashed rounded radii into a tabu set so that hops returning to an already-seen optimum are rejected without acceptance, forcing exploration of new basins.
backlog.title: Tabu-based swap of large and small circle roles

backlog.spec: Replace the time.time() based loop limits with fixed iteration counts (multistart: calibrated number of starts e.g. 60; basin hopping: fixed number of hops e.g. 600) while keeping seed 0, and keep a safety wall-clock cutoff at 230s. This makes the run reproducible and removes machine-load noise. Also reorder rng usage so multistart and hopping use separate Generators (default_rng(0) and default_rng(1)), so changing one phase does not alter the other.
backlog.title: Iteration-count budgets instead of wall clock

backlog.spec: Maintain a population of 6 elite distinct solutions during hopping (distinct if sorted radii differ by >1e-3). Every 20 hops, create a child by picking a random vertical or horizontal cut line at coordinate c in [0.3,0.7], taking circles with center on one side from parent A and the other side from parent B, then fix the count to 26 by deleting the smallest-radius circles in the overlap region or adding circles at random positions with small radius. Run SLSQP on the child and insert it into the population if it improves on the worst member. Run hopping from a randomly chosen elite member.
backlog.title: Basin hopping with population and elite crossover by region

backlog.spec: Solve the problem in a variable rectangle: add variables W and H, maximize sum r with walls at x in [r,W-r], y in [r,H-r], and the constraint W<=1+s, H<=1-s style via penalty fixed to W*H aspect trade, with the best result rescaled. Simpler: run SLSQP with a bound W=1+e, H=1/(1+e)... for e in {0.02,0.05,0.1}, then rescale the solution into the unit square by dividing centers and radii by max(W,H) and finish with a standard SLSQP polish from the scaled point. This gives basin-hopping new starting basins with different aspect ratios.
backlog.title: Rescaled-square free-boundary relaxation

backlog.spec: After basin hopping, identify active constraints (slack<1e-9) of the best solution. Solve the KKT system for sum r maximisation: use scipy.optimize.root on the square system formed by the equalities for active constraints plus stationarity with multipliers from lstsq of the gradient, iterating up to 20 steps. Accept the polished point only if all constraints are satisfied to 1e-13 after finalize and the sum increases. Aims to squeeze the last 1e-9 from the incumbent.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of the contact graph

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move (30% of hops) that keeps all centers fixed, multiplies each radius by a random factor in [0.5,1.0] for 3-6 randomly chosen circles (setting others to 0.9 of their current value), then runs SLSQP. This lets the optimizer re-balance radii between neighbours and escape degenerate rattler configurations without moving centers.
backlog.title: Radius-perturb-only hops

backlog.spec: Add a hop type (20%): delete one randomly chosen large circle (top 5 by radius), and place two circles of radius 0.5x the removed one at positions displaced by ±0.5*r along a random direction, while deleting the smallest circle elsewhere to maintain 26. Then run SLSQP. This targets structural changes in the big-circle skeleton rather than the small ones.
backlog.title: Remove the largest circle and re-grow

backlog.spec: In the penalty multistart, prepend a stage where the objective is -sum(r) plus lambda*sum(max(r - r_target,0)^2) with r_target drawn per start from uniform(0.09,0.12) and lambda=50, then drop it for the remaining mu stages. This biases starts toward uniform packings of different densities before releasing to size-variable optima, diversifying the basin set.
backlog.title: Elastic-net radius target warm-up

backlog.spec: Split the 200s into 8 independent chains each with seed i: 6s multistart then 19s basin hopping from its own best with sigma 0.03-0.06. After all chains finish, take the top 2 and run a final 20s of hopping with small sigma 0.01 from each. Contrasts with the single long chain by giving more global diversity at the same cost.
backlog.title: Multi-process-style split: 8 independent short chains with best-of

backlog.spec: Before the final SLSQP in each hop and multistart, run an SLSQP stage maximizing sum(r^p) with p=0.7 (rewarding smaller circles more, flattening size distribution) for 50 iterations, then switch to p=1. Variation in p reshapes the landscape and can move the solution to a neighbouring basin that the standard objective gets stuck outside of. Apply to 50% of hops.
backlog.title: Different objective exponent continuation

backlog.spec: Make no algorithmic change except to set the multistart cutoff to 60s and the basin-hopping cutoff to 200s as they are now. Add a final safeguard that re-verifies all pairwise and wall constraints in double precision and shrinks any violating radii by 1e-12 relative. This measures run-to-run repeatability and checks the validity code path.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent with time-based check

backlog.spec: Replace the wall-clock cutoffs with fixed counts: 150 multistart starts, then 1500 basin-hopping hops, with a safety wall-clock cap of 230s. Keep the current seed. This makes the result deterministic and independent of CPU speed, so the search does not lose hops when the machine is loaded.
backlog.title: Iteration-count budgets for basin hopping

backlog.spec: Keep a population of 6 distinct good optima from the multistart, found by deduplicating on sorted radii. Each generation, choose two parents and a random line through the square. Take the centers and radii of parent A on one side and parent B on the other. Fix the count at 26 by dropping the smallest circles or adding random ones, then repair with SLSQP. Replace the worst population member if the child is better and distinct. Run this for 80s before the final hopping.
backlog.title: Elite-population hopping with region crossover

backlog.spec: Optimise the packing in a square of variable side L, with L as an extra variable. Maximise sum(r)/L subject to the packing constraints in the L-sized square. Alternate this with fixing L=1 and rescaling the centers and radii by 1/L. This lets the whole configuration breathe during hops, so contact graphs can reorganise. Apply it as the first stage in 30% of hops, then finish with the standard unit-square SLSQP.
backlog.title: Free-boundary rescaled-square relaxation

backlog.spec: In 30% of hops, keep the centers fixed and multiply each radius by lognormal noise with sigma 0.15. Rescale the radii to be feasible, then run SLSQP with the standard settings. This explores the radius-size distribution without disrupting the geometry. The acceptance rule is unchanged.
backlog.title: Radii-only perturbation hops

backlog.spec: After hopping, identify the active constraints of the best solution, using a tolerance of 1e-9 on slack. Solve the equations for those constraints on the variables (x, y, r) as an exactly-determined or least-squares system using Newton iterations with numpy lstsq. Check feasibility, and accept the result only if the sum of radii does not drop. Then apply the 1e-10 shrink. This removes the residual SLSQP slack.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton refinement of the contact graph

backlog.spec: Divide the 200s into 8 rounds. In each round run 4 short chains of 6s each, each from a different seed, starting from the current elite solution with probability 0.5 and from a fresh multistart optimum otherwise. After every round, the elite becomes the best solution found so far. Use cheap neighbour-pruned SLSQP inside the chains, then do a full SLSQP re-polish of the elite at the end.
backlog.title: Eight short independent chains with elite restart

backlog.spec: After the basin hopping loop, take the best packing. Identify active constraints (pair gaps d-ri-rj < 1e-9 and wall gaps < 1e-9). Solve the KKT system with scipy.optimize.root or numpy lstsq: treat the active constraints as equalities in the variables (x,y,r), and take Lagrange multipliers from an LP/least-squares fit to the gradient of sum(r). Iterate Newton steps on the equalities to reach machine-precision contact. Then use the multiplier signs to drop any contact with a negative multiplier and re-run SLSQP once. Finally shrink radii by 1e-12 and keep the result only if the verified sum is higher than before.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish with exact contact solve

backlog.spec: Replace the single 60s multistart plus 140s hopping with 8 rounds. Each round runs a 6s multistart and then a 18s basin hopping chain from its own best, with a distinct seed. After each round, record the best. In the last 40s, run hopping from the global best only. Use a time check inside every loop so total runtime stays under 215s.
backlog.title: Eight short independent chains with elite restart

backlog.spec: Optimize in a square of side L as a variable. Add L as a variable in SLSQP with walls x-r>=0 and L-x-r>=0, maximizing sum(r)/L. Start L at 1.0 and let it drift during the first hops (e.g. L in [0.9,1.1]). After each hop, rescale all centers and radii by 1/L to get a unit-square packing. Use this as a smoother landscape in 50% of hops, then finish with a standard unit-square polish.
backlog.title: Free-boundary rescaled-square relaxation

backlog.spec: In 30% of basin hopping hops, remove two random circles (biased toward small radii). Compute the largest empty circle positions on the remaining 24 circles. Do this by sampling 4000 points on a grid and taking the points that maximise min(distance to the center minus its radius, wall distance). Take the best two well-separated points (at least 0.15 apart), insert the circles there with radii equal to the gap, then run SLSQP and accept via the existing rule.
backlog.title: Voronoi-vertex reinsertion of two circles

backlog.spec: Add a hop type (30%) that keeps centers fixed. Multiply each radius by lognormal noise (sigma 0.25), shrink radii until they are feasible, and then run SLSQP with maxiter 150 on the full problem. The idea is to move to different contact-graph basins without breaking the geometry. Accept using the existing criterion.
backlog.title: Radii-only perturbation hops

backlog.spec: Keep an elite pool of 12 distinct local optima from multistart and hopping (distinct means sum differing by more than 1e-4). Every few hops, choose two elites and a random line through the square at a random angle. Take the circles of parent A on one side and parent B on the other, then fix the count to 26 by dropping the smallest extras or adding circles at the largest hole. Polish with SLSQP and insert the result into the pool if it is good.
backlog.title: Elite-population region crossover

backlog.spec: Replace wall-clock loops in hopping with a fixed number of SLSQP hops (calibrate from the first 10 hops to fill about 140s). Every 50 hops, reset the current state to the best. Use a geometric temperature schedule from 0.003 down to 0.0002 over the run so that the early part explores and the end part is greedy.
backlog.title: Iteration-count budgeted hopping with periodic best reset

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP in hopping, read the multipliers from the result or estimate them by an NNLS fit of the gradient of sum(r) to the active constraint gradients. Find the active pair contact with the smallest positive multiplier. Push those two circles apart by 0.02 along their axis, plus a small random jitter, and re-polish. Accept if better. Run this as a deterministic phase on the best packing for the last 30s, iterating over all contacts in order of increasing multiplier.
backlog.title: Lagrange-guided weak-contact release

backlog.spec: As a bold move, in 20% of hops pick a random center point c and radius 0.25. Apply a radial map to centers inside it that expands (x -> c + (x-c)*1.3) for points near c and compresses the ones outside to keep the others within the square (clip). Set radii to 0.8x of the old values, and SLSQP-repolish. This emulates a local rearrangement of the contact network, like a vortex or dislocation shift.
backlog.title: Perturbation of row-count structure via inflation/deflation

backlog.spec: Replace wall-clock loops (60s multistart, 200s basin hopping) with fixed iteration counts calibrated to about 150s on the machine (e.g. time one SLSQP call first, then derive counts). Keep seed 0 and the same moves. This removes timing noise and lets the remaining budget go to extra hops. Stop at a hard 230s cap as a safety net.
backlog.title: Iteration-count budgeted deterministic run

backlog.spec: After a 30s multistart, run 8 independent basin-hopping chains of ~20s each, started from the top 8 distinct multistart optima (distinct by sum differing >1e-4). Each chain uses sigma 0.03-0.05 kicks of 1-4 circles. Then spend the remaining time hopping from the best chain result. Return the global best.
backlog.title: Eight short chains with elite restart

backlog.spec: Solve the packing in a square of side L as a variable: maximise sum(r)/L with SLSQP, with L bounded in [0.9,1.2] and walls at 0 and L. Then scale centers and radii by 1/L to fit the unit square. Use this in 30% of hops. The extra freedom lets the solver cross barriers. Always re-polish in the fixed unit square before scoring.
backlog.title: Free-boundary rescaled-square relaxation

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best packing and identify the active constraints (gaps <1e-7). Solve the KKT-like system of active equalities for centers and radii with a least-squares Newton iteration (scipy.linalg.lstsq). Accept the result only if the shrunken packing is valid and the sum improves. Use a final margin of 1e-12 and verify validity in double precision.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish with exact contact solve

backlog.spec: Add a hop type that keeps the centers and perturbs the radii by a lognormal factor (sigma 0.3). Scale them down to be feasible, then run SLSQP with a high iteration cap. This explores the contact-graph topology through the size distribution instead of positions. Use it in 25% of hops with Metropolis acceptance on the polished sum.
backlog.title: Radii-only perturbation hops

backlog.spec: In the penalty stage, add a smooth term -lambda*logsumexp(-k*r)/k that rewards larger small circles, with k=50 and lambda decaying from 0.05 to 0 over the mu stages. This is applied in 40% of multistarts. It biases the initial basins toward more uniform sizes before the final SLSQP polish on the true objective.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius warm start

backlog.spec: Before the final SLSQP, run SLSQP maximising sum(r^p) with p=0.5 first, then p=0.8, then p=1, warm-starting each stage from the previous result (maxiter 80 each). Concave early stages favour balanced radii and change which local optimum is reached. Use it in half of the multistarts and in the hop polishes.
backlog.title: Exponent continuation objective

backlog.spec: Run basin hopping at low sigma (0.02) with greedy acceptance. After 25 consecutive non-improving hops, apply a heat pulse: kick 6-8 circles with sigma 0.1 and polish, then continue greedily from that state for 15 hops. If it has not beaten the best, revert to the best. Repeat the cycle until 200s.
backlog.title: Periodic best-reset cycle with heat pulses

backlog.spec: Make no edit to train.py. Run the incumbent once more to check how repeatable -2.6360 is. The seed is fixed but the time-based loops can change the result. This tells us whether later gains are real or just timing noise.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Replace the wall-clock loops with fixed iteration counts. Run multistart for 120 starts and basin hopping for 1500 hops, with a time guard that stops at 230s. This makes the result deterministic for a given seed. Print nothing. Keep the rest unchanged, including the 1e-10 shrink margin.
backlog.title: Iteration-count budgeted basin hopping

backlog.spec: After basin hopping, take the best packing and find its active constraints, meaning pairs and walls with slack below 1e-9. Solve the square system of active equalities with a least-squares Newton iteration on (x, y, r). Use scipy.linalg.lstsq and run up to 10 iterations. Accept the result only if the objective does not drop after finalize. This removes the SLSQP tolerance error of about 1e-9.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton solve on contact graph

backlog.spec: Split the search into 8 rounds. Each round starts from the current elite, or from a fresh 10s multistart in the odd rounds. It then runs 15s of basin hopping with a seed that depends on the round. Keep the global best, and make the elite the best-so-far in the even rounds. This diversifies basins without losing progress.
backlog.title: Eight short chains with elite restart

backlog.spec: Optimize packings in a square of side L, where L is a variable with an upper bound of 1.2. The objective is sum(r) minus a penalty weight times (L-1), with the weight annealed from 0.5 to 10. Finish with a hard L=1 solve. Apply the scale 1/L to the centers and radii, then run SLSQP with L fixed at 1. Use this in 30% of multistart starts to smooth the landscape.
backlog.title: Free-boundary rescaled-square relaxation

backlog.spec: In 25% of basin hops, shrink every radius by 30%. Add a strong random displacement (sigma 0.03) to all centers. Run 30 iterations of the overlap penalty with radii growing back to the original, then SLSQP. This acts as a global shake that preserves the rough row structure but lets circles change neighbours.
backlog.title: Perturb row-count structure via inflation/deflation

backlog.spec: In 30% of basin hops, keep all centers fixed. Multiply the radii by lognormal(0, 0.3) noise, then shrink them to be feasible. Run SLSQP on all variables, then compare with the current state. This explores different contact graphs with the same centers.
backlog.title: Radii-only perturbation hops

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py except nothing functional (e.g. add a comment line at the top of construct_packing). Purpose is to measure repeatability of the -2.6360 result with the seeded run and confirm validity margin. Keep rng seed 0 and all timings.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Replace wall-clock checks in the basin-hopping loop with a fixed hop count (e.g. 900 hops) after a fixed number of multistart starts (e.g. 40), so the result is deterministic and independent of CPU speed. Add a wall-clock safety cutoff at 225s only as a guard. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Iteration-count budgeted basin hopping

backlog.spec: After the search, identify active constraints (pair gap<1e-9, wall gaps<1e-9) of the best packing. Solve the square or least-squares system gap_k(x,y,r)=0 for all active constraints with Gauss-Newton (np.linalg.lstsq, min-norm step) for up to 20 iterations, accept only if all constraints stay satisfied and sum improves, then apply the existing finalize shrink margin. Pure polish to squeeze 1e-10 level gains.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish with exact contact solve

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP on packings in a rectangle [0,W]x[0,H] with W,H as extra variables subject to W+H... fixed perimeter 2 (W=1+t, H=1-t, t variable in [-0.1,0.1]); then map the circles by affine rescale into the unit square (scaling radii by min scale), and polish with the standard unit-square SLSQP. Use this on 20% of multistart starts to reach different basins.
backlog.title: Free-boundary rescaled-square relaxation

backlog.spec: Keep a population of the 8 best distinct local optima from multistart. Create children by choosing a random vertical or horizontal cut line, taking circles left of the cut from parent A and the rest from parent B, then adjusting count to 26 by deleting smallest or adding at largest hole; SLSQP polish children; replace the worst population member if better. Run for 40s before basin hopping from the population best.
backlog.title: Elite-population region crossover

backlog.spec: In the penalty stage for half the multistarts, replace the -sum r objective at the first two mu values by -sum r + lam*sum(1/(r+0.02)) with lam=1e-4 decaying to 0, pushing toward balanced radii early, then proceed with the normal stages and SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius warm start

backlog.spec: Divide 200s into 8 rounds of ~25s. Each round starts from either the global best (rounds 5-8) or a fresh 6s multistart best (rounds 1-4), then runs basin hopping with sigma drawn per round from {0.02,0.03,0.05,0.08}. Keep the global best across rounds.
backlog.title: Eight short independent chains with elite restart

backlog.spec: In 30% of hops, keep centers of the current state fixed, solve an LP (scipy linprog, HiGHS) for max sum r with the objective perturbed by random weights 1±0.5, then take the solution as SLSQP start with true objective. This moves along the radius-degenerate directions of the contact graph.
backlog.title: Radii-only perturbation then re-solve with fixed centers LP

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, in 20% of hops: shrink all radii to 60%, scale center positions about (0.5,0.5) by 0.85-1.15 factor in one random axis plus gaussian jitter 0.02, clip to [0.02,0.98], then SLSQP. Acts as a compress/expand shake that rearranges rows.
backlog.title: Perturb row-count structure via inflation/deflation

backlog.spec: Before the final SLSQP in each multistart start and in 40% of hops, run SLSQP stages maximizing sum(r**p) for p=0.6 then 0.85 (maxiter 60 each, with gradient p*r**(p-1) using r clipped at 1e-6), then final p=1 polish. Concavity encourages more uniform radii, changing which basins are reached.
backlog.title: Exponent continuation objective

backlog.spec: Make no edits to train.py. The incumbent is deterministic only if wall-clock effects are absent, so this slot measures run-to-run variance (the loops are time-bounded). Return the file unchanged by replacing one comment line with an identical comment plus a trailing space, to keep the patch valid.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Replace the wall-clock stop in the basin-hopping loop with a fixed hop count of 400 hops, and replace the multistart wall-clock loop with a fixed 120 starts. This removes machine-speed nondeterminism. Keep the seed and all other logic. Add a hard time guard at 230s that breaks out of either loop, so a slow machine cannot time out.
backlog.title: Iteration-count budgeted basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a phase after multistart. Optimise a packing in a rectangle [0,w]x[0,1/w], which has the same area, where w is drawn from U(0.9,1.1). Use SLSQP with wall constraints that depend on w. Then map the centres and radii back to the unit square by a uniform scale of the best one, take that as a start, and polish it with the unit-square SLSQP. Run for 30s and keep the best result. Shorten basin hopping to match.
backlog.title: Free-boundary rescaled-square relaxation

backlog.spec: After basin hopping, identify the active constraints (slack below 1e-7) in the best packing. Solve this system with Newton/lstsq on the active equalities, which are the contacts and wall touches, along with the KKT multipliers from the LP dual. Then drop any contact with a negative multiplier, re-run SLSQP for 50 iterations, and keep the result only if the sum of radii improves after finalize. Use a final shrink of 1e-12.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish with exact contact solve

backlog.spec: In each multistart iteration, before the final SLSQP, run two short SLSQP stages with objective -sum(r^p) for p=0.6 then p=0.85 (maxiter 60 each, analytic gradient -p*r^(p-1)). The concave stage pushes toward equalised radii. Then run the true p=1 objective polish. Guard r with a 1e-6 floor in the gradient. Apply to 50% of starts.
backlog.title: Radius-power objective continuation

backlog.spec: In 25% of basin hops, take the best state, sort its circles by radius, and permute the radii so that they are assigned to different centres. Swap radii between two random neighbouring circles, then shrink all radii by 20% so the start is feasible. Run SLSQP as usual. This tests topology changes that a kick of centres cannot make.
backlog.title: Hop-time hole-filling by radius-sorted reassignment

backlog.spec: For 30% of multistart starts, put 4 corner circles at (0.1,0.1) etc. with r=0.1. Add 12 evenly spaced circles on the inset boundary at distance 0.09 from the walls, with r=0.09. Place the remaining 10 as a jittered pentagon-ring pair (5 at radius 0.18 from centre, 5 at 0.32) with r=0.1. Add jitter sigma 0.01 and run the SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Edge-heavy symmetric ring seeds

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, for each hop generate 6 kicked candidates. Score each by running SLSQP for only 15 iterations. Then fully polish just the best-scoring candidate (maxiter 100). Use the usual Metropolis acceptance on the polished result. This raises the effective search width at a modest cost.
backlog.title: Cheap SLSQP pre-screen of kicks

backlog.spec: Replace wall-clock loops with fixed iteration counts calibrated so total runtime is about 200s (e.g. a 60s multistart measured once, then fixed hop count). Keep the seed fixed so results are exactly repeatable. Before the hops, time one SLSQP hop and compute the hop count as (190s - elapsed)/hop_time, then run exactly that many hops. This removes timing noise and lets us compare seeds fairly.
backlog.title: Iteration-count budgeted deterministic basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add SLSQP variables for the square side L (bounds 0.9-1.15) with walls at 0 and L and objective sum(r)/L. Run it from the incumbent's best and from top multistart optima, then rescale centers and radii by 1/L into the unit square. Finally re-polish with the standard unit-square SLSQP. This lets the structure relax along a scale-invariant path and can escape the tight local optimum.
backlog.title: Free-boundary rescaled-square relaxation

backlog.spec: After basin hopping, identify active constraints (slack<1e-9) in the best solution. Solve the nonlinear system of active contacts with a Newton/least-squares iteration, using scipy.optimize.root or least_squares, over the variables not in rattlers. Then compute the LP-optimal radii for the resulting centers and shrink by 1e-12 relative. Accept only if the sum improves and the packing is valid.
backlog.title: Exact active-set KKT vertex solve

backlog.spec: In 30% of hops, keep the centers fixed, perturb the objective weights of an LP over radii (maximise sum w_i r_i with w random in [0.5,1.5]) to reach a different vertex of the radius polytope, then run SLSQP on the true objective from there. Use scipy linprog HiGHS. This explores degenerate vertices that plain kicks miss.
backlog.title: Radii-only LP-guided hop

backlog.spec: Split the time into 8 chains of about 23s. Each chain starts from a fresh 4s random multistart best, then runs basin hopping with its own seed. After each chain, store the result. For the final 15s, run basin hopping from the best of all chains. Output the global best.
backlog.title: Many short independent chains with elite restart

backlog.spec: In the penalty stage objective, add +beta*softmin(r) with a smooth temperature of 0.01 and beta decaying from 0.3 to 0 across the mu stages. This pushes toward more uniform radii at first. For 40% of multistarts use beta>0; the rest use the original. Final SLSQP polish is unchanged.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius warm-up regularization

backlog.spec: Initialise from a perfect hexagonal lattice with spacing s sampled in [0.17,0.21], randomly rotated by 0-30 degrees and offset, clipped to the unit square. Keep points with margin at least 0.04. Take exactly 26 of them: delete the extras randomly or add random points in the largest holes. Use radii 0.5*s*0.9, then run SLSQP. Use this for 40% of multistarts.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-plus-defect big-seed lattice init

backlog.spec: Use 4 corner circles fixed at the corner-touching positions (x=r, y=r) with free radii. Constrain them in SLSQP via equal-position bounds, and place the other 22 randomly with radius 0.09. Optimise, then release the corner constraint and polish. Run for a 40s phase before the main multistart.
backlog.title: Seed sweep by structured corner circles

backlog.spec: Optimise 24 circles with SLSQP multistart for 20s, then add two circles at the largest holes found via a grid-sampled distance field with initial radius 0.02. Re-optimise with SLSQP, then run the standard basin hopping from the best. Repeat the ladder with n=25 plus one circle in a second phase of 20s.
backlog.title: Bold: lower-n then insert-and-grow ladder

incumbent.description: Shorten multi-start to 60s, then basin hopping (perturb 1-4 centers, sigma 0.05, SLSQP maxiter 100, Metropolis T=0.002) until 200s with fixed seed.

memo: Helped: only the optimizer family. Slot 0 (multi-start penalty L-BFGS-B plus SLSQP polish) moved loss from 0.9598 to -2.6343. Slot 1 (60s multistart plus basin hopping) reached -2.6360, the incumbent, above the best known 2.635. Slots 2-144 gave no gain. Nearly all tied at -2.6360 or fell back to -2.6343. Tried without gain: init variants (corner, lattice, row, Lloyd), symmetry (14, 44, 47, 76), reinsertion moves, contact-pair, affine and sinusoidal moves, weighted objectives, radius-cap and sum(r^p) stages (144), pair-pruned SLSQP, pool crossover (99, 107), split-budget multi-seed chains (77, 87, 96, 109), trust-constr, Newton and LP polishes. Other seeds gave -2.6343 (25, 72) or tied (95, 130). Worse: slots 13, 75, 19, 32, 62, 68, 102, 122, 125, 36, 105, 118, 124, 140. Keep the shrink margin (slot 11 fell back to -2.6343). Many proposals were aborted as repeats. The search looks stuck at -2.6360. Next: stop proposing init or move variants. Run one replicate of the incumbent to check repeatability, or accept -2.6360.
